I was a little boy, in 4th or 5th grade, and was helping my step father with a burn pile. Showed me what to do to set it up and let me light it. As I started igniting the top of the pile he told me to stop. He didn't tell me what to do he just asked me a question.

Which way does the fire burn? Look at the lighter.

Up?

Yes. So where should you start the fire to make it burn?

The bottom.

So I changed what I was doing after he taught me how to think about the situation. He didn't tell me what to do, he taught me how to observe and think about it for myself.

I'm sure I've had other experiences in the meantime, but every time I have to figure something out for myself I think "The fire always burns up"

Not important, just a story.

Thanks for sharing :) My earliest critical thinking memory is also with my dad, only I was detangling a set of cables in the back of his truck.
